# introduction
Read the guidelines at .github/copilot-instructions. You have the role of reviewer, you will write plans for analyzer and then start an analyzer subagent to carry out that those plans. It is up to you how to schedule and send off the tasks to analyzer subagent(s), but keep the work of each subagent isolated. Be careful of recompiling executables which might be in use by another program. If there is a chance a file is being edited or executable ran or will soon-to-be ran by anther subagent, then wait until that subagent's task has concluded. For analysis production use 20-30 threads, for skimming use 5 threads for mc and 10 threads for data.

## pPb to Pbp Z reweighting
 - Z weight here was not calcualted correctly in the last task. Calculate the weight over the Z pT range 0-500 using the raw Z pPb and Pbp data skims as input. When applying the weight to Pbp the Z pT and Z eta distributions should close with good agreement with the pPb distributions. When looking at the zcorr slides produced, there is still the same bin-to-bin jumpy differences between the histograms. These should be flattened out as much as possible. Ensure the correction was actually applied as well since the histograms dont seem to change beteen presentations. If so then investigate why the Z data correction did not close between the data distributions, and recalculate it. Prove that the closure is legit by showing a plot where ratio Pbp/pPb is near flat. Here are the original instructions which should be repeated with the fix in place:
```
In the sandbox, calculate a test Z residual correction as a function of three variables which scales the pPb data (Z pT, Z eta, Z phi) distributions to match those of the Pbp data (Z pT, Z eta, Z phi) distributions. Copy parts of framework of the iterative correction proceadure used in 20260115_ZCorrection to the sandbox so we can modify them without messing with the main analysis. Calculate the correction factor iteratively and store the factor in the sandbox.

Create a new flag for the sandbox CorrelationAnalysis which when activated will read-in the Z corrections and apply them to pPb (pPb ONLY! not Pbp). Upon application of the weights, the distributions of Z pt and Z y made previously should match near exactly between pPb and Pbp data.

Make a completely new presentation with the weights applied to pPb based on the Z-unweighted presenation that includes coparison between Pbp and weighted pPb
 - trk eta
 - trk pt
 - Z y
 - Z pt
 - event multiplicity
 - Z-track (delta eta, delta phi) ratio map
 - Z-track delta eta correlation
 - Z-track delta phi correlation
 - Z-track delta R correlation

And for each of these include 6 levels of corrections as done before:
For six levels of corrections: 
 - no corrections, no EventWeight, no TrackWeight
 - only VZ correction
 - VZ correction + Z correction
 - VZ correction + Z correction + Z scale factor
 - VZ correction + Z correction + Z scale factor + TrackWeight
 - VZ correction + Z correction + Z scale factor + TrackWeight + TrackResidual

Compute each of these histograms for all 6 levels of corrections AND for nominal pile up and PU reject cases. Keep the plotting and analysis contained to the sandbox and do not override anything in the official weight dictionary.
```

# conclusion
Make the minimum number of edits necessary to implement functionality. Do not add superflous error statement catches or checks. 

Have the subanalyzer handoff a summary to you and you should review that summary for flaws. Update copilot instructions on the new norms detailed here and learned by you or the subanalyzer throught these tasks.
